holidays.name: Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day
holidays.description: A tip of the Stetson to country songs with wonderfully odd, hilarious, and heartbreakingly literal titles. Spend the day queuing up tunes about pickup trucks, exes, and everything in between, and see how many titles make you laugh before the first chorus.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, kept alive by country fans and music lovers who enjoy the genre's talent for wordplay and storytelling.
holidays.funFact: Country music is famous for long, punny titles, and songwriters have been known to start with a clever title and then build the whole song around it.

holidays.name: National Spanish Paella Day
holidays.description: A celebration of Spain's iconic rice dish, cooked in a wide, shallow pan and loaded with saffron-scented rice, vegetables, and seafood or meat. It's a perfect excuse to gather friends around a big pan and dig in.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. The dish itself comes from the Valencia region of Spain, where it began as a hearty meal for farmers and laborers.
holidays.funFact: The word paella is commonly linked to the name of the pan it's cooked in, and the crispy toasted layer of rice at the bottom, called socarrat, is considered the prize of the dish.

holidays.name: World Theatre Day
holidays.description: A global salute to the stage, celebrated by theatres, performers, and audiences in countries around the world with performances, festivals, and special events. Curtain up on drama, comedy, musicals, and everything in between.
holidays.origin: It was established in 1961 by the International Theatre Institute and has been celebrated every year since. Each year a notable theatre figure writes an international message to mark the day.
holidays.funFact: The tradition of an annual World Theatre Day message means a different theatre luminary from somewhere in the world gets to address the global theatre community every March 27.
